## Q1 | A Monopoly on Brooms

Before its method for broomstick manufacturing spread, SwiftTech was the only maker of the standard broom. Its costs are the ones from Homework E2: a fixed cost of 360 coins a week, with a marginal cost of:

$$
MC = 5 + \frac{Q}{5}
$$

where $Q$ is the number of brooms it makes in a week. As the only seller it faces the whole market’s demand and charges the same price for every broom. Demand and marginal revenue are:

$$
D: P = 53 - \frac{Q}{5} \qquad\qquad MR = 53 - \frac{2Q}{5}
$$

The table shows its average total cost at some quantities. Each graph shows demand, marginal cost and average total cost.

::: {.table style=grid density=compact columns="auto 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr" fills=r0:gray-dark valign=middle}

| **Brooms** | **40** | **60** | **80** | **120** |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **ATC** | 18 | 17 | 17.5 | 20 |

:::

:::: {.columns gutter=0.5em}

::: {.column width=60%}

SwiftTech picks its quantity and price:

a\) Graph marginal revenue ($MR$).

::: solution

$MR = 53 - \frac{2Q}{5}$ starts at 53 with demand and falls twice as fast: it is 21 at 80 brooms and reaches zero at 132.5.

:::

b\) Find and graph the profit-maximizing quantity ($Q^*$).

::: solution

$MR = MC$: $53 - \frac{2Q}{5} = 5 + \frac{Q}{5}$, so $48 = \frac{3Q}{5}$ and $Q^* = 80$ brooms.

:::

c\) Find and graph the price that sells that quantity ($P^*$).

::: solution

Go up to demand at 80 brooms: $P^* = 53 - \frac{80}{5} = 37$ coins.

:::

d\) Find and graph SwiftTech’s maximized profit.

::: solution

At 80 brooms $ATC$ is 17.5, so profit is $(37 - 17.5) \times 80 = 1{,}560$ coins: the rectangle between the price and $ATC$, out to 80.

:::

:::

::: {.column width=40%}

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

:::

::::

:::: {.columns gutter=0.5em}

::: {.column width=60%}

There are no externalities:

e\) Find and graph the socially efficient quantity.

::: solution

Marginal benefit equals marginal cost where demand crosses $MC$: $53 - \frac{Q}{5} = 5 + \frac{Q}{5}$, so $Q = 120$ brooms.

:::

f\) Find and shade the deadweight loss.

::: solution

At 80 brooms buyers pay 37 and the marginal cost is $5 + \frac{80}{5} = 21$. The triangle between demand and $MC$ from 80 to 120 is $\frac{1}{2}(37 - 21)(120 - 80) = 320$ coins.

:::

g\) Buyers would pay more than the marginal cost for the next broom after $Q^*$. Why doesn’t SwiftTech make it?

::: solution

To sell one more broom it has to lower the price on every broom it sells. Past 80 brooms that leaves marginal revenue below marginal cost, so its profit would fall.

:::

:::

::: {.column width=40%}

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

:::
